prompt: Same material, right after studying it — two different measurements of "do I know this":

options.label: How confident you feel after rereading
options.content: High. The material feels familiar, the explanation made sense as you followed it, nothing felt confusing. This confidence is real, but it's measuring fluency - how smoothly the material processed the second time you saw it - which is a different thing from whether you could produce it yourself without it in front of you.

options.label: How you'd actually score, closed-book, right now
options.content: Often noticeably lower than the confidence predicted. Without the material in front of you, gaps show up that rereading never surfaced - partial recall, details that seemed "obviously" understood but can't actually be reconstructed. This is the real measurement; the confidence from rereading was never a reliable stand-in for it.
